pages.title: 4.2 Python scripting
pages.text: Lesson 4.2: Foundations of Isaac Sim Scripting With Python (Isaac Sim 6.1) # Course page: Developing Robots With SIL → Foundations of Isaac Sim Scripting With Python ( …/04-foundations-of-isaac-sim-scripting-with-python.html ) Goal: create the same scene (physics + ground + falling cube) three ways: USD API, the Isaac Sim Core API, and a standalone script. Files: scripts/m4_snippet_usd_api.py , scripts/m4_snippet_core_api.py , scripts/m4_run_snippet.py Expected result: with either snippet the cube falls from z = 1.0 and rests at z = 0.25. 🎬 Narrated walkthrough · lesson ⏱ 45 min · caption text (.srt) · download .mp4 You will learn to Run code in the Script Editor and as a standalone app Choose between raw USD and the 6.1 core API Port 4.x omni.isaac.core code The Python layers you script against — interactive HTML Concepts # Two ways to run Python. Script Editor : inside the running GUI, shares its stage — good for poking. Standalone ( ./python.sh my.py ): your script owns the app loop via SimulationApp , can run headless, and is how tests, data generation and RL run. Rule #1 of standalone scripts. Create SimulationApp(...) before importing anything from isaacsim.* / omni.* (those modules only exist once Kit is running). Which API? Raw pxr USD is verbose but never changes between versions. isaacsim.core.experimental is concise and batched (operate on many prims at once, NumPy/Torch/Warp arrays) — the 6.x way. Part 1: Script Editor (unchanged) # Window > Script Editor. Run or Ctrl+Enter runs the whole tab. Select some lines and use Run Selected to run only those. Tab > Add Tab opens more tabs. All tabs share one Python environment, so a variable defined in one tab is visible in the others. Part 2: USD API workflow (course code works as-is ✅) # File > New . Paste scripts/m4_snippet_usd_api.py into the Script Editor → Ctrl+Enter . A ground plane and a cube appear. Play , and the cube falls. pxr ( Usd , UsdGeom , UsdPhysics , PhysxSchema ) is the stable foundation under Isaac Sim. Code written against it keeps working across versions. Run it once per empty stage . Part 3: Isaac Sim Core API workflow (🔄 rewritten for 6.1) # The course's code doesn't run in 6.1 : # ❌ 4.2 course code: omni.isaac.core no longer exists in 6.1 from omni.isaac.core.objects import DynamicCuboid from omni.isaac.core.objects.ground_plane import GroundPlane from omni.isaac.core.physics_context import PhysicsContext The 6.1 equivalent ( scripts/m4_snippet_core_api.py ): from isaacsim.core.experimental.materials import PreviewSurfaceMaterial from isaacsim.core.experimental.objects import Cube , GroundPlane from isaacsim.core.experimental.prims import GeomPrim , RigidPrim from pxr import UsdPhysics import omni.usd stage = omni . usd . get_context () . get_stage () if not any ( p . IsA ( UsdPhysics . Scene ) for p in stage . Traverse ()): # = PhysicsContext() UsdPhysics . Scene . Define ( stage , "/World/PhysicsScene" ) GroundPlane ( "/World/groundPlane" , sizes = 10 ) cube = Cube ( "/World/cube" , sizes = 1.0 , positions = [ - 0.5 , - 0.2 , 1.0 ], scales = [ 0.5 , 0.5 , 0.5 ]) material = PreviewSurfaceMaterial ( "/World/Looks/cube_color" ) material . set_input_values ( "diffuseColor" , [ 0.2 , 0.3 , 0.0 ]) cube . apply_visual_materials ( material ) RigidPrim ( cube . paths ) # makes it dynamic (= "DynamicCuboid") GeomPrim ( cube . paths , apply_collision_apis = True ) # gives it a collider What changed: 4.2 / 4.5 6.1 Note DynamicCuboid(...) (shape + physics in one) Cube(...) + RigidPrim(...) + GeomPrim(..., apply_collision_apis=True) 6.1 splits geometry , rigid body and collider into separate wrappers position=np.array([...]) positions=[...] 6.1 wrappers are batched : plural argument names, and they accept lists of paths color=np.array([...]) a PreviewSurfaceMaterial + apply_visual_materials PhysicsContext() a UsdPhysics.Scene prim (or isaacsim.core.simulation_manager.SimulationManager ) Steps: File > New From Stage Template > Empty → Don't Save → paste → Ctrl+Enter → Play . Part 4: Standalone Python (bonus, not in the course) # Real SIL setups usually run Isaac Sim from a script, not the GUI. Every file in scripts/ is a standalone app: from isaacsim import SimulationApp # 4.2: from omni.isaac.kit import SimulationApp simulation_app = SimulationApp ({ "headless" : False }) # must come BEFORE any other isaacsim/omni import import omni.timeline # ... build the stage ... omni . timeline . get_timeline_interface () . play () while simulation_app . is_running (): simulation_app . update () # one rendered + simulated frame simulation_app . close () Run a Script Editor snippet as a standalone app: ./python.sh learning_resource/scripts/m4_run_snippet.py learning_resource/scripts/m4_snippet_core_api.py ./python.sh learning_resource/scripts/m4_run_snippet.py learning_resource/scripts/m4_snippet_usd_api.py --headless --test More 6.1 examples to read next: File (under standalone_examples/ ) Shows api/isaacsim.simulation_app/hello_world.py the smallest possible app api/isaacsim.core.experimental.api/add_cubes.py rigid bodies, materials, resetting state api/isaacsim.core.experimental.api/control_robot_numpy.py articulation control with the 6.1 API api/isaacsim.ros2.bridge/subscriber.py rclpy inside Isaac Sim tutorials/getting_started/getting_started_robot.py loading and moving a robot Check your result # Do this You should see USD snippet in Script Editor + Play cube falls and rests at z = 0.25 Core API snippet in Script Editor + Play same m4_run_snippet.py … --headless --test [m4] PASS: cube fell … Exercises # Extend the core-API snippet to create 10 cubes in a row with one Cube(...) call (pass a list of paths and positions). Turn m4_snippet_core_api.py into a standalone script that prints the cube height every 10 frames. Read standalone_examples/api/isaacsim.core.experimental.api/add_cubes.py and explain RigidPrim.set_velocities . Quiz # What must be the first Isaac Sim import in a standalone script? Answer `from isaacsim import SimulationApp`, then create it. 4.x DynamicCuboid in 6.1? Answer `Cube` + `RigidPrim` + `GeomPrim(apply_collision_apis=True)`. Which layer's code survived 4.2 → 6.1 unchanged? Answer Raw OpenUSD (`pxr`) code.

pages.title: 4.3 Camera images for Isaac ROS
pages.text: Lesson 4.3: Publish camera images for Isaac ROS # Your robot software needs to see the scene before it can interpret it. In this lesson, publish Nova Carter's camera and check that an external ROS 2 viewer receives the images. Finish line for this page: a live camera image in rqt_image_view . Running a segmentation model is an external continuation, not a result established by this camera check. The existing video also introduces that wider workflow. 🎬 Narrated walkthrough · lesson ⏱ 20–30 min estimated for the camera check; allow additional time for external Isaac ROS setup · caption text (.srt) · download .mp4 You will learn to Publish simulated camera images to ROS 2 Identify the camera feed needed by an external Isaac ROS pipeline Software-in-the-loop with Isaac ROS — interactive HTML Concepts # Camera graphs. A camera publisher needs a render product (the camera rendered at a resolution); the ROS 2 Camera tool creates it plus the publisher nodes for RGB, depth, segmentation or boxes. Containers and distros. Isaac ROS runs in Docker, often on Humble. DDS lets Humble and Jazzy exchange standard messages if RMW and domain ID match; when in doubt, run Isaac Sim with the same distro. Course pages: Developing Robots With SIL → Foundations of Image Segmentation, ROS 2, and Isaac ROS · Image Segmentation Without Simulation · Image Segmentation With Simulation These lessons run Isaac ROS (a Docker-based ROS 2 workspace) next to Isaac Sim. Most of the work happens in Isaac ROS, so follow the course pages for that part. Only the Isaac Sim side changes: What changes on the Isaac Sim side # Course 6.1 ROS 2 Humble everywhere Isaac Sim publishes with its bundled Jazzy libs. ROS 2 talks across distros at the DDS level for standard messages ( sensor_msgs/Image , CameraInfo ), but keep the same RMW ( rmw_fastrtps_cpp ) and ROS_DOMAIN_ID on both sides. If the Isaac ROS container is Humble and messages don't arrive, launch Isaac Sim with the container's distro: export ROS_DISTRO=humble before ./isaac-sim.sh (6.1 bundles both humble and jazzy libs under exts/isaacsim.ros2.core/ ) Camera → ROS graph built by hand or via Isaac Utils > ROS2 OmniGraphs > Camera 🔄 Tools > Robotics > ROS 2 OmniGraphs > Camera . Pick the camera prim and tick RGB (+ optional Depth, Semantic, Instance, BBox). Topics default to rgb , depth , … with Frame ID sim_camera Nova Carter cameras Same asset ( Create > Robots > Nova Carter with Sensors ). Hawk/Owl cameras live under chassis_link/sensors/… Quick check: camera to ROS 2 # Scene from lesson 4.1 (Nova Carter in the Simple Room). Tools > Robotics > ROS 2 OmniGraphs > Camera → Camera Prim = e.g. /World/nova_carter/chassis_link/sensors/front_hawk/left/camera_left , tick RGB , OK. Play , then: bash source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash ros2 topic hz /rgb ros2 run rqt_image_view rqt_image_view /rgb A scripted version of this graph is in standalone_examples/api/isaacsim.ros2.bridge/camera_periodic.py (run it with ./python.sh ). Continue to model inference # Use the Image Segmentation Without Simulation and Image Segmentation With Simulation lessons in the original NVIDIA learning path for the Isaac ROS environment and model setup. Return to this feed once inference works on the example input used there. For that continuation, keep an RGB frame and the model's predicted mask side by side. Record the input/output topics and describe at least one visible mistake. Simulator-generated semantic labels are ground truth from the scene; they are not evidence that a segmentation model ran successfully. Check your result # Do this You should see ros2 topic hz /rgb a steady rate while playing rqt_image_view /rgb the Hawk camera image Exercises # Also publish depth and view it in RViz as an Image display. Lower the camera resolution in the dialog and compare /rgb rates. Quiz # What does a camera publisher need besides the camera prim? Answer A render product. Isaac ROS on Humble, Isaac Sim on Jazzy, no messages — one fix? Answer Launch Isaac Sim with `ROS_DISTRO=humble` (bundled) and matching RMW/domain.

pages.title: 5 Hardware-in-the-loop
pages.text: Module 5: Leveraging ROS 2 and Hardware-in-the-Loop (notes for Isaac Sim 6.1) # 🎬 Narrated walkthrough · lesson ⏱ reading 15 min (hands-on needs a Jetson) · caption text (.srt) · download .mp4 You will learn to Explain hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) Prepare the Isaac Sim side for a Jetson Hardware-in-the-loop deployment — interactive HTML Concepts # HIL vs SIL. In SIL the robot software runs on your workstation; in HIL it runs on the robot's real computer (Jetson), so you also test its timing, GPU load and networking — without risking the robot. Simulated time. The simulator may run slower or faster than real time. Publishing /clock and setting use_sim_time: true on the Jetson keeps every node on the simulator's clock. Course pages: Leveraging ROS 2 and HIL in Isaac Sim : HIL fundamentals, Jetson overview, Jetson environment setup, deploying Isaac ROS on Jetson. This module is mostly about the NVIDIA Jetson board (JetPack, Isaac ROS containers). Isaac Sim plays the same role it did in Module 4: it publishes sensor topics and subscribes to /cmd_vel . You need Jetson hardware to do it hands-on, so there's no checkpoint script. Isaac Sim side: what to keep in mind with 6.1 # Network: the Jetson and this PC must share a network, the same ROS_DOMAIN_ID and the same RMW ( rmw_fastrtps_cpp by default). Test with ros2 topic list on the Jetson while Isaac Sim is playing. ROS distro: JetPack/Isaac ROS images are often Humble. If Jazzy (Isaac Sim) ↔ Humble (Jetson) messages don't arrive, start Isaac Sim with export ROS_DISTRO=humble (bundled libs for both distros are in exts/isaacsim.ros2.core/ ). Sim time: add a clock publisher ( Tools > Robotics > ROS 2 OmniGraphs > Clock , or standalone_examples/api/isaacsim.ros2.bridge/clock.py ) and set use_sim_time: true on the Jetson nodes. Graphs: reuse lesson 4.1 ( /cmd_vel ), lesson 1.4 (lidar) and lesson 4.3 (camera). The menu paths are all under Tools > Robotics > ROS 2 OmniGraphs in 6.1. Navigation (Nav2): 6.1 ships ready-made scenes: Window > Examples > Robotics Examples → ROS2 > Navigation , e.g. carter_warehouse_navigation.usd . Follow the course pages for the Jetson setup itself (JetPack, Docker, Isaac ROS). Check your result # Do this You should see On the Jetson: ros2 topic list Isaac Sim's topics (clock, scan, rgb) On the Jetson: ros2 topic hz /clock steady rate while Isaac Sim plays Exercises # Without a Jetson: run the 'Jetson side' in a second terminal (or Docker) on the same PC with use_sim_time:=true and check it follows /clock . Quiz # What does use_sim_time: true do? Answer Nodes use the /clock topic instead of the wall clock. Two settings that must match on both machines? Answer ROS_DOMAIN_ID and the RMW implementation.

pages.title: All diagrams
pages.text: All diagrams Click a diagram to open its interactive, zoomable HTML version. Course map: five modules, one robot story Course map showing Isaac Sim 6.1 feeding five modules: first robot, URDF import, synthetic data, software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop, each with its main artifact. Lesson 1.1 — from a mesh to a driving robot Six steps that turn plain meshes into a driving robot: meshes, physics scene, rigid bodies, revolute joints, angular drives and an articulation root. Lesson 1.1 — SimpleRobot, seen from above Top view of SimpleRobot: the Cube chassis is body 0 of four revolute joints whose body 1 is a wheel; the two rear wheels carry the angular drives. Lesson 1.2 — the Differential Controller graph Action Graph built by Tools > Robotics > OmniGraph Controllers > Differential Controller: keyboard keys become linear and angular velocity, the controller turns them into wheel speeds and the articulation controller drives the rear joints every frame. Lesson 1.3 — where to mount each sensor in 6.1 Decision flow for mounting sensors on SimpleRobot in Isaac Sim 6.1: cameras and the deprecated PhysX lidar may sit on the fixed-jointed Front_Sensor body, but an RTX lidar must sit directly under the chassis body and above the wheel tops. Lesson 1.4 — RTX lidar to RViz over ROS 2 Data path built by Tools > Robotics > ROS 2 OmniGraphs > RTX Lidar: the playback tick renders the RTX lidar into a render product, the ROS2 RTX Lidar Helper publishes a LaserScan on /scan_lidar, and RViz2 draws it. Lesson 2.1 — URDF to a drivable USD robot Pipeline for importing Carter in Isaac Sim 6.1: the URDF goes through File > Import with Base Type Mobile, becomes carter.usda with payloads and a Physics variant set, the physx variant must be selected and the wheel drives configured before a controller can move it. Lesson 2.1 — what the 6.1 importer writes Hierarchy of the imported carter.usda: links live under Geometry with chassis_link as articulation root, joints live under Physics, and a Physics variant set chooses the engine layer. Lesson 2.2 — where the controller numbers come from The Differential Controller parameters for Carter come straight from the URDF: wheel radius 0.24 m from the wheel cylinder and wheel distance 0.6284 m from the joint offsets; keyboard input then drives left_wheel and right_wheel through the articulation controller, clamped to 0.5 m/s. Lesson 2.3 — sensors on the imported Carter Camera and RTX lidar mounted directly under Carter's chassis_link body; the camera feeds a viewport, the lidar sees every rendered obstacle, and colliders on the obstacles only matter for physical contact. Lesson 2.4 — Nova Carter's ready-made sensor suite Hierarchy of NVIDIA's Nova Carter in Isaac Sim 6.1: chassis_link is the articulation root carrying two 2D lidars, an XT-32 3D lidar, four Hawk stereo cameras, four Owl fisheye cameras, and the driven and caster joints. Module 3 — pallet-jack dataset with Replicator (6.1) Synthetic data pipeline: load the warehouse, add pallet jacks and distractors, keep labels only on pallet jacks, set up camera and KittiWriter, then per frame randomize with the functional API, step the orchestrator and write a KITTI dataset used to train a detector. Lesson 4.1 — driving Nova Carter from /cmd_vel ROS 2 to Isaac Sim control loop: teleop_twist_keyboard publishes geometry_msgs/Twist on /cmd_vel, the Action Graph subscribes, splits linear.x and angular.z, the Differential Controller computes wheel speeds and the Articulation Controller drives joint_wheel_left and joint_wheel_right. Lesson 4.2 — the Python layers you script against Layer stack of Isaac Sim 6.1 scripting: your script on top of isaacsim.core.experimental, Kit and omni services, OpenUSD pxr APIs and the PhysX and RTX engines; omni.isaac.core is removed and isaacsim.core.api deprecated. Lesson 4.3 — software-in-the-loop with Isaac ROS Software-in-the-loop setup: Isaac Sim publishes a Hawk camera image on /rgb through the ROS 2 Camera graph, an Isaac ROS segmentation container processes it, and your ROS node can send /cmd_vel back to the drive graph. Module 5 — hardware-in-the-loop with a Jetson Hardware-in-the-loop deployment: the workstation runs Isaac Sim 6.1 with ROS 2 graphs, a LAN carries DDS traffic with matching ROS_DOMAIN_ID and RMW, and the Jetson runs Isaac ROS and your perception or Nav2 nodes using simulated time, sending /cmd_vel back.
